artworks.title: Ilissus
artworks.description: Burrow’s romantic view of the Athenian Ilissus — the stream Hyginus lists among Oceanus’ river-sons and beside which Boreas seized Orithyia. Landscape art keeps the river-god’s watercourse when his human face is rare.

artworks.title: Boreas and Oreithyia
artworks.description: Louvre K35: Boreas abducts Orithyia — the myth Apollodorus and Apollonius set on the banks of the Ilissus. The vase stages the river’s most famous story even when the water-god himself stays off the clay.

artworks.title: Boreas Abducting Oreithyia
artworks.description: Rubens’ Baroque storm of the north wind carrying Erechtheus’ daughter — the Ilissus abduction as European salon myth. The Athenian river remains the named stage of the rape that links Boreas to Attica.

popCulture.title: Ilisos
popCulture.description: Athenian river-god and stream — setting of Boreas’ rape of Orithyia, and in Plato’s Phaedrus the shady bank of philosophical talk.
